evidence.reason: `wait_ssh` establishes a `deadline` from its `timeout` argument for the SSH polling loop, but once SSH succeeds it launches `cloud-init status --wait` with a fresh hard-coded 240-second timeout rather than the remaining readiness budget. A first SSH success near the end of the window can therefore make the function run for nearly 2x its timeout before failing, so callers cannot rely on the supplied timeout as a bound. Capping the nested call (and polling attempts) to the remaining deadline is a routine correctness fix, not an owner-level behavior change.
